Life is the most extraordinary phenomenon in the known universe; but how does it work? Even in this age of cloning and synthetic biology, the remarkable truth remains: nobody has ever made anything living entirely out of dead material. Life remains the only way to make life. Are we missing a vital ingredient in its creation?  
  
Like Richard Dawkins' _The Selfish Gene_ , which provided a new perspective on evolution, _Life on the Edge_ alters our understanding of life's dynamics as Jim Al-Khalili and Johnjoe Macfadden reveal the hitherto missing ingredient to be quantum mechanics. Drawing on recent ground-breaking experiments around the world, they show how photosynthesis relies on subatomic particles existing in many places at once, while inside enzymes, those workhorses of life that make every molecule within our cells, particles vanish from one point in space and instantly materialize in another.  
  
Each chapter in _Life on the Edge_ opens with an engaging example that illustrates one of life’s puzzles – How do migrating birds know where to go? How do we really smell the scent of a rose? ## Description

In "Life on the Edge: The Coming Age of Quantum Biology," Jim Al-Khalili and Johnjoe Mcf introduce readers to a captivating intersection of biology and quantum mechanics that challenges our fundamental understanding of life itself. This groundbreaking work explores how the principles of quantum theory influence biological processes, from photosynthesis and sensory perception to the intricate workings of the avian navigation system. With a blend of accessible science and intriguing anecdotes, Al-Khalili and Mcf invite us to reconsider the very essence of life, suggesting that at the microscopic and subatomic levels, the mysteries of biology may hold secrets yet to be unveiled. As we journey through this fascinating realm, we are compelled to ponder: could the very fabric of life be woven from the fabric of the quantum world? Dive into this thought-provoking exploration that promises to transform your perception of life and the universe.
